column1: # Japanese grammar words and endings. One line per word as written + part of speech:
# word <TAB> UD part of speech <TAB> senses separated by " | ".
# The file replaces Wiktionary's determiner, pronoun, preposition, conjunction,
# particle and auxiliary entries for every word listed here; content words stay.
# The analyzer (`context.analyzer` in language.toml) splits a clicked verb into
# its morphemes (勉強|し|て|い|ます), and each ending shows its line here, found
# by its spelling first (でしょう, たら), else by its base form (です, た). A
# word written in kana that Wiktionary only
# redirects to its kanji spelling (つまり -> 詰まり) is found through the
# redirect; lines here are for what Wiktionary lacks or says badly.
# Each sense explains what the word does, for a learner reading it next to
# the sentence: what it expresses, then the English, then a short phrase in
# brackets when the English alone doesn't settle it ("who you do something
# with: go with a friend (友達と行く)"). No notes on case or position: the sentence
# shows those. A casual or short form names its full form and links it:
# "(casual form of てしまう) ... → てしまう".

column3: makes a verb polite: eat (食べます)
past: the action or state is over: ate (食べた) | already done, finished by now: have already eaten (もう食べた)
closes a statement, plainly and firmly; polite speech uses です: he's a student (学生だ) → です | the past ending た, spelled だ after some verbs: read (読んだ) → た
closes a statement politely, where plain speech uses だ: I'm a student (学生です) → だ | after an い-adjective, only makes it polite: it's expensive (高いです)
(polite form of だろう) a guess: probably: it'll probably rain (雨でしょう) → だろう | checks that the listener agrees: you get it, right? (分かるでしょ)
a guess: probably, I suppose: it'll probably rain (雨だろう) | checks that the listener agrees, bluntly: you know that, right? (知ってるだろ)
once this happens, what follows: if you go, when you go (行ったら) | did it, and then found, often to your surprise: I woke up and it was raining (起きたら雨だった)
names a few actions as examples, among others: eating, drinking and so on (食べたり飲んだり)
joins a verb to what comes next; the actions happen one after another: eat and sleep (食べて寝る) | how or why something happens: came on foot (歩いて来た), was late because it rained (雨が降って遅れた)
the action is going on right now: is eating (食べている) | the state an action left behind: is married (結婚している)
(casual form of ている) going on now, or its result is still there: is eating (食べてる) → ている
not: the verb's negative: doesn't eat (食べない) | ないで: without doing it, or asking someone not to: without telling (教えないで), please don't go (行かないで)
want to, of yourself; for others Japanese uses たがる: I want to eat (食べたい)
(casual form of てしまう) happened against your will, often with regret: I forgot (忘れちゃった) → てしまう | done completely, nothing left: ate it all up (食べちゃった)
ちゃう after verbs whose て form ends in で: read it all (読んじゃった) → ちゃう
(casual form of ては) doing it would be bad: you mustn't eat it (食べちゃだめ) → ては | なくちゃ: have to: I have to go (行かなくちゃ) → なくちゃ
doing it would be bad; usually followed by だめ or いけない: you mustn't eat it (食べてはだめ) | again and again, one after the other: writing and erasing, over and over (書いては消す)

passive: something is done to the subject, often unpleasantly: be told (言われる) | can do it: casual speech drops the ら of られる after ichidan verbs and 来る: can eat (食べれる) → られる | respect: says politely what someone else does: the teacher writes (先生が書かれる)
passive: something is done to the subject: be eaten (食べられる) | とされる: is said to be, is considered | can do it: can eat (食べられる) | respect: says politely what someone else does: comes (来られる)
makes or lets someone do it; the context tells which: make him go, let him go (行かせる)
makes or lets someone do it: make them eat, let them eat (食べさせる)
your will, or an invitation: let's eat, I'll eat (食べよう); ようとする: try to, be about to (しようとする) | 様: how something seems, like, as if: it's like a dream (夢のようだ)

column1: ## Forms of endings, shown as one segment (言え|なかった, 食べ|てい|ます)
# A run of endings whose spelling, or whose last ending in its base form,
# has a line here is one segment, with the line's senses (endingGroup in
します/しました/しません/しませんでした/しましょう
column3: (polite form of する) do, did, don't, let's do: I study (勉強します) → する
if that's so, taking it as given: if you're going (行くなら) | picks something as the topic: when it comes to Japanese food, sushi (日本料理なら寿司) | それなら: in that case, then
(casual form of なければ) have to: I have to go (行かなきゃ) → なければ | if you don't, unless: you won't know unless you try (やらなきゃ分からない)
(casual form of なくてはいけない) have to: I have to go (行かなくちゃ) → なくてはいけない
didn't, wasn't: the past of ない: didn't go (行かなかった) → ない
if not, unless: a form of ない: if you don't go (行かなければ) → ない | なければならない, なければいけない: must, have to: I have to go (行かなければならない)
not, and: a form of ない, often giving the reason: I didn't understand, so ... (分からなくて) → ない | なくてもいい: you don't have to: you don't have to go (行かなくてもいい)
the past of ます: did it, said politely: ate (食べました) → ます
not, the polite ます form: don't eat (食べません) → ます
didn't, the polite ます form: didn't eat (食べませんでした) → ます
was, were: the past of です: was a student (学生でした) → です
was, were: the past of だ: was a student (学生だった) → だ
wanted to: the past of たい: wanted to eat (食べたかった) → たい
the action is going on right now: is eating (食べている) | the state an action left behind: is married (結婚している) | something done regularly, as a habit or job: works at a bank (銀行で働いている)
do it now, ready for later: buy it in advance (買っておく) | leave it as it is, on purpose: leave it open (開けておく)
happened against your will, often with regret: I forgot (忘れてしまった) | done completely, nothing left: ate it all up (食べてしまった)
do it to see what it's like or what happens: try eating (食べてみる)
a change that has come about up to now: it has got cold (寒くなってきた) | go, do it and come back: go and buy it (買ってくる)

a change or action that goes on from now: will keep increasing (増えていく) | one after another, going forward: let's look at them in turn (順番に見ていきましょう) | do it and go away, or take it with you: take along (持っていく)
(casual form of ておく) do it ahead, or leave it as is: buy it in advance (買っとく) → ておく
someone does it for me or for us, as a favour: he taught me (教えてくれた)
I get someone to do it for me, as a favour: I had her teach me (教えてもらった)
I do it for someone, as a favour: I'll teach you (教えてあげる)

column1: # X: only adds, so な keeps Wiktionary's particle entries (行くな, "don't").
# に of 確かに: an adverb, shown after the adjective's entries (labelled
# "adverb") in place of だ "is", which UniDic's lemma would give.

column3: turns a な-adjective into an adverb: quietly (静かに)
joins a な-adjective to its noun: a quiet room (静かな部屋)

joins nouns into a complete list, unlike や, which names only some: a dog and a cat (犬と猫) → や | who you do something with: go with a friend (友達と行く) | marks what was said or thought, like closing quotation marks: said he'd go (行くと言った) | whenever this happens, that follows: it opens when you push it (押すと開く)

(casual form of と) marks what was said or thought: said he'd go (行くって言った) → と | picks a topic to say something about, casually: humans are scary (人間って怖い) | passes on what you heard: I hear it'll rain (雨だって) | called, named: a person called Tanaka (田中って人)
but, because: gives a reason, often as an excuse: but I don't want to (だって嫌だもん) | even, too: even a child understands (子供だって分かる) | passes on what you heard: I hear he's going (行くんだって)
(casual form of じゃないか) ..., right?, expecting agreement: I told you (言ったじゃん)
but, although: it was expensive, but I bought it (高いけれど買った)

things like, such as: gives a loose example | kind of, like: a filler that softens what follows: kind of strange (なんか変) | something: eat something (なんか食べる) | makes light of a person or thing: someone like me (私なんか)

how, what, in surprise: how beautiful (なんてきれい) | what, in a question: what did he say? (なんて言った?) | names something lightly, often dismissively: things like, the likes of: studying and all that (勉強なんて)
wondering aloud: I wonder if I can go (行けるかな) | with ない, a wish: I wish he'd come soon (早く来ないかな) | (literary) in haiku, marks wonder or admiration
about, around, with an amount: about three hours (三時間ぐらい) | so much that: so painful you could cry (泣くぐらい痛い) | at least, just: a small amount taken as the minimum: at least this much (これぐらい)
about, around, with an amount: about three hours (三時間くらい) | so much that: so painful you could cry (泣くくらい痛い) | at least, just: a small amount taken as the minimum: at least this much (これくらい)
from, since: a letter from Tokyo (東京からの手紙)

column1: にわたって/にわたる/にわたり
column3: over a whole stretch of time or space: over three years (3年にわたって)
according to: names where the information comes from: according to the news (ニュースによると)
according to: names where the information comes from: according to the survey (調査によれば)
by: names who did it, in a passive sentence: written by him (彼によって書かれた) | depending on: differs from person to person (人によって違う) | because of, due to: due to the typhoon (台風によって)
by, caused by, due to: damage from the earthquake (地震による被害) | depending on
about, regarding, in formal speech: regarding this matter (この件に関して)
about: a book about the environment (環境に関する本)
toward, to: the person or thing an attitude is aimed at: toward customers (客に対して) | against: against the government (政府に対して) | compared with, for each: two for every one (一に対して二)
toward, against, of: criticism of the government (政府に対する批判)
only, nothing more than; plays it down: it's only a rumor (噂にすぎない)
must be, surely: a confident guess: it must be true (本当に違いない)
not only ... but also: not only in Japan but abroad too (日本だけでなく海外でも)
(casual form of だけでなく) not only ... but also: not only cheap but tasty (安いだけじゃなくおいしい) → だけでなく
is not: the negative of だ: is not a student (学生ではない) → だ
(casual form of ではない) is not: isn't a student (学生じゃない) → ではない | isn't it?: said with rising voice, expecting agreement: isn't it nice (いいじゃない)
not this, but that: not red but blue (赤ではなく青)
(casual form of ではなく) not this, but that: not red but blue (赤じゃなくて青) → ではなく
you know, isn't it?: politely expects the listener to agree: it's important, isn't it? (大事じゃないですか)
explains, gives the background: the thing is, you see (行くんです) | んですか: asks for an explanation: what happened? (どうしたんですか)
explains, or gives the background, more formally than んです: the thing is, you see (行くのです) → んです | のですか: asks for an explanation
んです after a noun: the thing is, you see (学生なんです) → んです
(casual form of んです) explains, or gives the background: I'm going, you see (行くんだ) → んです | んだって: passes on what you heard

as, the way: as I said before (前に言ったように) | so that: aiming at a result: so as to be in time (間に合うように) | ようにする: make a habit of, make sure to (早く寝るようにする) → ようにする | ようになる: come to, a change that happened little by little (話せるようになった) → ようになる
therefore, for that reason: what follows is the result of what came before
besides, on top of that: adds one more point: and besides, it's cheap (それに安い) | to that, on that: answer that (それに答える)
until then: wait until then (それまで待つ) | that's all, the end of it
turns to what matters more: never mind that, more importantly (それより、どうする?) | than that: bigger than that (それより大きい)
so, at that point: what was done because of what just happened: so I thought about it (そこで考えた) | there, at that place: meet there (そこで会う)
that kind of, such: about what was just said, or near the listener (そういう人)
this kind of, like this: about something near you, or about to be said: at times like this (こういう時)
that kind of: about something away from both of you, or known to both: a person like that (ああいう人)
what kind of, how: what does it mean? (どういう意味)

column1: # Phrases Wiktionary lacks. A line here may start at an ending inside a word
# (ようとする in 出よう|と|した), which a Wiktionary phrase may not.

column3: it was decided, not by you, or it turns out: I'm to go (行くことになった)
decide to, by your own choice: I decided to go (行くことにした)
can, more formally than the short form (泳げる): can swim (泳ぐことができる)
sometimes, it happens that: I sometimes go (行くことがある) | have done it before, at least once: have been there (行ったことがある) | there is something that: there's something I haven't said (言ってないことがある)
try to, or be just about to: tried to leave, was about to leave (出ようとした)
come to: a change that happened little by little: became able to speak (話せるようになった)
make a point of, make sure to: make sure to go to bed early (早く寝るようにする)
must, have to: an obligation, said formally or in writing: I have to go (行かなければならない)
must, have to: I have to go (行かなければいけない)
must, have to: I have to go (行かなくてはいけない)
(casual form of なくてはいけない) must, have to: I have to go (行かなくちゃいけない) → なくてはいけない
(casual form of なければいけない) must, have to: I have to go (行かなきゃいけない) → なければいけない
may, it's all right to; asks for or gives permission: you may eat (食べてもいい) | なくてもいい: you don't have to
(casual form of てもいい) may, it's all right to: may I eat? (食べていい?) → てもいい

column1: と言っていい/といっていい
column3: you could say, it's fair to say: it can fairly be called a success (成功と言っていい)
must not: forbids it: you must not eat (食べてはいけない)
(casual form of てはいけない) must not: you mustn't eat (食べちゃいけない) → てはいけない
can't, because it wouldn't be right, though nothing stops you: I can't very well take the day off (休むわけにはいかない)
a conclusion that makes sense of things: so that's why, no wonder: so that's why he was late (だから遅れたわけだ) | explains how things stand: this is how it is (こういうわけです)

column1: わけではない/わけじゃない
column3: it's not that, not necessarily: it's not that I dislike it (嫌いなわけではない)
there's no way, it can't be: no way (そんなわけがない)
so, for that reason: so, that's why (そういうわけで)
what you expect from what you know: should: he should come (来るはずだ)
intend to, plan to: your own intention: I intend to go (行くつもりだ)
should, it would be good to: asks for or gives advice: what should I do? (どうすればいい?)
had better: advice: you'd better go (行ったほうがいい) | is better, comparing two: smaller is better (小さいほうがいい)
had better: advice: you'd better go (行った方がいい) | is better, comparing two: the other one is better (他の方がいい)
in this way, like this: sums up how something happened

called, named: a person called Yamada (山田という人) | that: gives what a noun says: the forecast that it will rain (雨が降るという予報) | というか: or rather, I mean | というのは, というのも: the thing is, that's because | と + 言う: says that: he says he'll go (行くという) → 言う
the fact that, that: that he'll go (行くということ) | that is to say, which means

column1: ## Constructions with する and なる
# お…する and the like have a word in them: `context.analyzer.constructions`
# in language.toml finds them, and shows the line named here.

column3: humble: you lower yourself to honour the listener: I'll wait (お待ちします)
respectful: raises the person who does it: he writes (お書きになる)
please do, asked politely: please wait (お待ちください)
choose, decide on: I'll have coffee (コーヒーにする) | make it so, turn it into: be quiet (静かにする) | treat as, use as: treat with care (大切にする)
make it more so: make it cheaper (安くする)
there is a sound, smell or taste that you notice: there's a sound (音がする) | 気がする: have a feeling that | がされる: something is done: an explanation is given (説明がされる)

suppose, if we assume: supposing we go (行くとすると) | treat as, regard as; とされる: is regarded as (名作とされる) | state, hold that: they say that (としている) | after a word for how something looks or feels, be like that: solid (しっかりとした)
surprisingly: more or less than you expected: surprisingly easy (意外と簡単)
rather than, or rather: a better way to put it: more shouting than talking (話すというより叫ぶ)
in a sense, in a way: right in a sense (ある意味正しい)

column1: はっきり言って/はっきりいって
column3: frankly, to be honest: comes before a blunt opinion: frankly, it's impossible (はっきり言って無理だ)
almost, nearly: almost every day (ほぼ毎日) | about, roughly
as expected, after all: it rained after all (やはり雨だった) | still, also, likewise: he too (彼もやはり)
(casual form of やはり) as expected, after all → やはり | still, also | well, I think: a filler before an opinion
gradually, little by little: it gradually gets colder (だんだん寒くなる)
really, truly; makes what follows stronger: thank you so much (本当にありがとう)
very, extremely, in formal speech: extremely important (非常に重要)
a little, a bit: wait a moment (ちょっと待って) | rather, a bit: softens something negative: a bit difficult (ちょっと難しい) | said alone, a polite way to refuse: that's a bit ...
well, um: a filler, often letting something go: well, whatever (ま、いいか)
well, um: a filler, often letting something go: well, whatever (まあ、いいか) | oh my!, in surprise | more or less: so-so (まあまあ)
uh, um: a filler while thinking | eh? what?: surprise, or not having heard
ah, oh: noticing something: oh, right (あ、そうだ) | uh: hesitating
which: which book (どの本) | with も, every; with でも, any: every carp (どの鯉も), anyone (どの人でも)
this way, this direction | here: this way please (こちらへどうぞ) | this one; also, politely, I or we, or the person here
